chosen.premise: When Bulbasaur is young, it grows by using nutrients stored in the seed on its own back.
chosen.hook: Before Bulbasaur grows up, its seed feeds it.
chosen.visualIdea: An x-ray-style animation sends nutrient particles from Bulbasaur’s back seed through its body as it grows taller.
chosen.note: A distinctive biological contradiction—its back seed nourishes it—supported by three consistent entries and easy to show with an internal nutrient animation.

candidates.premise: Bulbasaur begins life with a strange seed already planted on its back, and that plant grows alongside it.
candidates.hook: Bulbasaur is born with something planted in its back.
candidates.visualIdea: A baby Bulbasaur silhouette reveals a seed on its back, then a split-screen timelapse shows both body and seed growing.
candidates.note: A defining Bulbasaur premise, strongly supported across multiple Pokédex entries, with an immediately visual birth-and-growth reveal.

candidates.premise: Bulbasaur naps in bright sunlight, and the sun’s rays make the seed on its back progressively larger.
candidates.hook: Bulbasaur’s nap time is also growing time.
candidates.visualIdea: A sleeping Bulbasaur naps under a moving sun; each beam fills a growth meter and enlarges the seed.
candidates.note: Strong visual transformation and official support, though sunlight-driven growth is a narrower variation on the broader seed premise.

candidates.premise: Bulbasaur’s entire three-stage line advances on a clean level pattern: evolve at 16, then again at 32.
candidates.visualIdea: A level bar hits 16 to transform Bulbasaur into Ivysaur, then races to 32 for Venusaur, with 16 → 32 highlighted.
candidates.note: The 16-to-32 pattern is concrete and well supported, but evolution-level patterns are not especially unique to Bulbasaur.

candidates.premise: Bulbasaur keeps the exact same Grass/Poison type pairing through every stage, from #001 to #003.
candidates.hook: Bulbasaur evolves twice—but never changes its type combo.
candidates.visualIdea: Bulbasaur, Ivysaur, and Venusaur slide in as #001, #002, and #003, each stamped with identical Grass and Poison badges.
candidates.note: Clear and screen-friendly, but unchanged typing across an evolution line is a comparison format that can apply to many Pokémon. (Uniqueness capped at 2: its evidence is only fields every Pokémon has.)

candidates.premise: Bulbasaur can go days without food because the bulb on its back stores energy.
candidates.hook: Bulbasaur can skip meals for days—because of its back.
candidates.visualIdea: A day counter climbs from Day 1 to Day 3+ while the glowing bulb acts like an energy battery meter.
candidates.note: The energy-storage mechanic is interesting and visual, but “days” is not quantified and the premise rests on one entry.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; born-with-a-seed is the best episode premise. A stronger alternative would need a more surprising, uniquely Bulbasaur contradiction or quantified mechanic while retaining equally direct Pokédex support.
